name: Radio Telescope
desc: An array of parabolic dish antennas standing on a ridge, slowly slewing in azimuth and nodding in elevation to track across the sky while an unseen light rakes the panelled reflectors; the dishes stand along a lower band and leave the sky open — cool brushed steel, a dusk rim-lit silhouette, thermal false-colour, an engraving, or a schematic.

energy.doc: how brightly the light rakes the metal and the amplitude of the slew

scale.doc: dish size — min a distant far-off array, max huge foreground dishes

density.doc: how many dishes stand in the array (3 to 6)

speed.doc: how fast the dishes slew and nod

sweep.doc: how fast the raking light drifts across the reflectors

x.doc: centre of the array across frame

y.doc: ridge line height so the sky above stays open

style.doc: aesthetic: cool brushed steel raked by light / a dusk rim-lit silhouette against a glowing sky / thermal false-colour / a cyan schematic / a hatched engraving plate

seed.doc: array lottery — per-dish depth, placement and slew phase

alpha.doc: layer opacity — scales every mark so it dissolves into the background rather than veiling it
